locator.text: Equation (C.5), p. 159, in the proof of Lemma C.1

evidence: paper: t(\theta'; \mu) \;=\; t_s + d_0 \, \frac{e^{\mu p_{s,2} \sin \theta'} / M_e(\mu p_{s,2}) - 1}{p_{s,2}}, \qquad \mu \ge 0.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Term by term with m = t_s, d = d_0, p = p_{s,2}: `expTilt` is m + (d/p)(e^{μp cos θ}/M_e(μp) - 1), and d_0 · (e^{·}/M_e - 1)/p_{s,2} = (d_0/p_{s,2})(e^{·}/M_e - 1), so the two agree up to the same sin→cos translation of the angular origin recorded for (C.4). Two encoding points, neither a mathematical difference. (i) The paper restricts μ ≥ 0 in (C.5); the Lean definition is for all real μ, and the sign restriction reappears where it is used (`solveScale_nonneg`, `tiltVariance_strictMonoOn` on `Ici 0`). (ii) The paper's removable singularity at p_{s,2} = 0, with value t_s + d_0 μ sin θ', is not carried by `expTilt` itself (whose `d / p` is Lean's junk value 0 at p = 0, giving the constant m); it is carried by `extendedExpTilt`, which is defined by a case split to be cosineTilt m (dμ) = m + dμ cos θ at p = 0, exactly the paper's value, and by `regularizedTilt`, a denominator-free formula proved equal to it. I did not trace whether the smoothness in p across p = 0 that the paper gets from G(p)/p = ∫_0^1 G'(up) du is proved for this family here; that argument belongs to the surrounding prose rather than to this block.
